old_caption:
The video captures a dramatic scene set in a forest. The sky is overcast with clouds, creating a somber backdrop for the unfolding event. In the center of the frame, a large plume of dark smoke rises into the air, indicating a significant explosion or collapse. Surrounding the smoke, debris is being propelled upwards and outwards, consisting of various sizes of rocks and pieces of wood. These fragments scatter across the scene, some landing on the ground while others continue to ascend.

The trees in the background are mostly bare, suggesting it might be winter. Some evergreen trees are visible on the right side of the frame, providing a contrast to the otherwise barren landscape. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on capturing the dynamic movement of the debris and smoke. The overall atmosphere is one of chaos and destruction, with the natural elements of the forest juxtaposed against the unnatural force of the explosion.

caption:
The video captures a low-angle, upward view through a bare woodland. Pale deciduous trunks and dark evergreen branches frame an overcast white sky. A tall vertical column of dark clumped debris already fills the center of the view from the first instant. Irregular black and brown chunks hang suspended within a brownish smoky haze that crowns the top, partly hiding the thin birch trunks behind them.
Throughout the sequence the plume remains airborne, its internal arrangement shifting continuously as individual clumps move turbulently among the tree trunks behind them. Some larger clumps linger near the base of the column, while finer particles veil the surrounding branches. As the sequence advances, the left and right margins of the cloud grow more diffuse, with scattered chunks spreading outward. The upper haze softens in turn. The background trees and sky stay visible, while the composition evolves mainly through the spread and repositioning of the suspended debris.

trace.prompt:
Audit this candidate caption against the actual chronological images, and correct factual errors.
This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

Return JSON {"decision":"keep|edit", "issues":[{"quote":"exact span in candidate caption",
"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

draft_caption: The video captures a low-angle, upward view through a winter woodland. Bare deciduous trunks and snow-dusted evergreen branches frame an overcast white sky. A tall vertical column of dark clumped debris already fills the center of the frame from the first instant. Irregular black and brown chunks hang suspended within a brownish smoky haze that crowns the top. Throughout the excerpt this plume remains airborne, its internal arrangement shifting continuously as individual clumps drift turbulently against the tree trunks behind them. As the sequence advances, the left and right margins of the cloud grow more diffuse, with scattered chunks spreading outward. The upper haze thickens and softens in turn. The camera slowly pans and tilts, carrying the prominent leaning birch trunk on the right progressively toward the frame's edge and repositioning the evergreen foliage and sky background accordingly. No new object enters or exits; the composition of trees, sky, and suspended debris is maintained, evolving only in spread and framing.
